item.title: Sarah Sze’s Artful ‘Constellations’ Invite Wonder and Inclusion

item.title: Rembrandt’s Refugees
item.description: A timely exhibition of work by the Dutch master shows centuries-old art amid the new gloss of an incendiary political issue.
item.dc:creator: Nina Siegal

item.title: Van Gogh Soars to $190.4 Million at Sotheby’s After an 11th-Hour Settlement
item.description: In less than a week, the painting went from top lot to top liability — and back again. On Wednesday it set a record for the artist.
item.dc:creator: Julia Halperin and Zachary Small

item.title: 30 Years Ago, Robert A.M. Stern Asked New York to Preserve These Modern Buildings
item.description: Two from the architect’s 1996 list of 35 have been demolished. Here’s what happened to the rest of the structures Stern sought to protect.
item.dc:creator: Fred A. Bernstein
item.category: Huntington Hartford Gallery of Modern Art
item.media:credit: Daniel Terna for The New York Times
item.media:description: 2 Columbus Circle is now the Museum of Arts and Design, Edward Durell Stone’s marble facades replaced by iridescent terra-cotta tiles by Allied Works Architecture.

item.title: Contested Frida Kahlo Painting Is Withdrawn Hours Before Auction
item.description: Christie’s withdrew the work after accusations that several of the artist’s paintings had gone missing from the Casa Azul house-museum in Mexico City.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Burnett
item.media:credit: Banco de México Diego Rivera Frida Kahlo Museums Trust, Mexico, CDMX/Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York; Photo by Cindy Ord/Getty Images
item.media:description: Christie’s removed a Frida Kahlo painting, “Congreso de los pueblos por la Paz (Congress of Peoples for Peace),” from an auction Tuesday. It depicts a dove perched in a fruit tree flanked by nuclear mushroom clouds.

item.title: Jewish Heirs and Consignors Settle Claim Over $180 Million van Gogh Ahead of Sale
item.description: Already the top lot of the season, the van Gogh became the center of controversy after a claim surfaced that it was sold under Nazi-era duress in the 1930s.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Hickley and Zachary Small
item.media:description: “Châtaigniers en Fleurs (Blossoming Chestnut Trees),” from 1890, is to be sold Wednesday at the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection Evening Auction at Sotheby’s.

item.title: Trump’s Culture War, Amid Setbacks, Will Soon Face a Hostile Congress
item.description: The White House campaign to make major changes at the Smithsonian and the Kennedy Center has fallen short of its goals. Will it be further disrupted by a Democrat-led Congress?
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Robin Pogrebin
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Caroline Gutman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Efforts to control personnel and presentations at the Smithsonian Institution have been among President Trump’s cultural initiatives during his second term.

item.title: As Phillips Scales Back, the ‘Big Two’ Auction Houses Seem to Stand Alone
item.description: Phillips was always an underdog in the auction world, but it had ambition to compete with Christie’s and Sotheby’s. Then the economics changed.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small and Julia Halperin
item.media:credit: Graham Dickie for The New York Times
item.media:description: Many of the executives who oversaw Phillips’s heyday five years ago have left the company.

item.title: Birthplace of Many Marvel Superheroes? The Mind of a Lower East Side Boy.
item.description: Jack Kirby helped create Iron Man, the Hulk and many other superheroes who went on to great crime-fighting careers and starring roles in movies and TV shows.
item.dc:creator: George Gene Gustines

item.title: At the Alta Center, Chicano Art and Activism Walk Hand in Hand
item.description: The Alta, a new free public art space near downtown Los Angeles, holds a collection of Latino art infused with the spirit of the Chicano civil rights movement.
item.dc:creator: Carolina A. Miranda
item.media:credit: Jennelle Fong for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Alta in Montebello, Calif., opens Sunday with a major collection of Chicano, Latino and Mexican art. Above, an exhibition “LA LA LA” by the photographer Patssi Valdez.

item.title: Doubts Loom Over a van Gogh as Auctions Aim for a $2.8 Billion Week
item.description: Major paintings by Cézanne, Picasso and Klimt are positioned to entice collectors as Sotheby’s seeks resolution for the auction’s most coveted painting. Five bellwether works to watch.
item.dc:creator: Tim F. Schneider, Zachary Small and Julia Halperin

item.title: At Sotheby’s, Risk-Taking Left a $180 Million van Gogh in the Lurch
item.description: Claims on the painting by heirs of a Jewish owner were well known in the art world. The auction house will meet lawyers for the heirs on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Small
item.media:description: Visitors to Sotheby’s in Hong Kong in October looked at Vincent van Gogh’s “Châtaigniers en Fleurs (Blossoming Chestnut Trees),” ahead of its auction in New York.

item.title: Hitting Art Hard With Innovation
item.description: The very existence of a show devoted to “Black abstraction” raises questions. Is it valid to continue to sort art by identity? On the evidence of “Hard Art,” the answer is yes.
item.dc:creator: Holland Cotter and Guarionex Rodriguez

item.title: Art Gallery Shows to See in November
item.description: This week in Newly Reviewed, Jillian Steinhauer covers a little-known government arts era, Mary Lovelace O’Neal’s visceral abstractions and a group exhibition of 99 tiny works.
